text:
Danila Yurov's second NHL season has made him two things at once: one of Minnesota's goal scorers and a name in trade talk. With Dylan Larkin refusing to play for Detroit until he is traded, reports have linked the Wild to the Red Wings captain with Yurov in the package, and NHL.com wrote that general manager Bill Guerin "plays coy" when asked about it.

On the ice, the 22-year-old has 9 goals in 22 games, already close to the 12 he scored all of last season, and his ice time has grown to about 16 minutes a night. Two of those goals came in Boston on Nov. 14. The chances are real: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 89th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season.

The finishing is not. He is scoring on 26% of his shots, against 15% last season, with 9 goals on 5.7 expected, and his linemates have also scored well above their chances with him on the ice. A finishing rate like that rarely lasts. He missed practice on Nov. 16 with what NHL.com's Heather Rule called a maintenance day.
headline: Danila Yurov's breakout has put his name in Larkin talk
